Scientific name: Trichomycterus auroguttatus Costa, 1992.

Size: 61 mm SL.

Type locality: Rio Marimbondo, tributary of Rio Preto, Rio Paraiba basin, 1 kilometer west of Visconde de Mauá, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Etymology: Trichomycterus comes from the Greek trichos, meaning hair, and mykter, meaning nose; in reference to the barbels.

IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
South America: Marimbondo River, tributary of the Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin. Rio de Janeiro State.
South America: Marimbondo River, tributary of the Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin.
Marimbondo River, tributary of the Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin (Costa et al. 2022).
This genus takes live or frozen food, as well as commercial dry prepared foods. Be careful not to overfeed. In nature, they feed on small invertebrates living at the bottom.

Will feed on most aquarium fare such as tablet, frozen and live foods. It is an opportunistic predator that mainly feeds on insects, but also will take small crustaceans and plant material (algae and remains of phanerogams).

Etymology: The specific name auroguttatus: aureus (L.), golden; guttatus (L.), spotted, referring to golden spots (alternating with dark spots) on posterior half of body, and a row of gold spots on midline of back, behind dorsal-fin base.

Trichomycterus auroguttatus is endemic to the Paraíba do Sul basin, being rare and not very abundant. It occurs in an area impacted by urbanisation, which apparently does not represent a significant threat that puts its population at risk, being categorised as Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2022).
Revue française d'Aquariologie Herpétologie v. 18 (no. 4) [for 1991], pp 105, Fig. 6.
